recent_facts: The IKEA Effect explains why we irrationally overvalue our own work, a bias that can be neutralized by asking if we would choose our current projects if we hadn't started them ourselves.
The Chainstore Paradox reveals that irrational aggression can be a rational long-term strategy to deter future competitors.
The "Madman Theory" proves that sometimes appearing irrational to your opponents is a more effective deterrent than showing your hand.
The Dutch Tulipomania bubble is a historical myth; it was a small, niche trade that never caused a national economic collapse.

The "Great Filter" theory suggests that civilizations either pass a near-impossible evolutionary bottleneck or go extinct, placing our current technological trajectory in a high-stakes, cosmic context.
